claims.head: The Hurricanes feed on mistakes, and the Capitals make them
claims.call: The Hurricanes get at least their usual 7.8% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Hurricanes turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Capitals are the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Capitals.
claims.nums: Carolina 2nd for chances off turnovers (7.8% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Washington 32nd for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Hurricanes pounce on loose pucks, and the Capitals cough them up.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 4 games this season

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 expected goals within 5 seconds of winning the puck
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Capitals should get some good looks
claims.call: The Capitals’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Capitals make their shots count, and the Hurricanes are the league’s worst at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Capitals to get some real chances.
claims.nums: Washington 6th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Carolina 32nd for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Capitals make their shots count, and the Hurricanes allow dangerous ones.

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals

claims.head: The Hurricanes kill penalties far better than the Capitals
claims.body: On the penalty kill, Carolina is one of the league’s best and Washington is near the bottom of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.gist: The Hurricanes and the Capitals sit at opposite ends for penalty kill.
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Capitals’.

check.measure: expected goals allowed per 60 on the penalty kill
check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: M. Roy is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. T. Liljegren has taken his spot beside J. Chychrun.
S. Jarvis has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. W. Carrier has taken his spot beside S. Aho and A. Svechnikov.
L. Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: J. Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 68% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 61 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by N. Ehlers (15 of 18 changes).

CAR.head: Carolina has nearly everything going for them
CAR.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Washington can make a game of it if they get good looks.

WSH.head: Washington has their work cut out
WSH.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Washington could still pull it off if they get good looks, but they might need a miracle.

story.head: Round two in Carolina
paras: The Capitals already came to Carolina once this season and left with a 5-2 win. The Hurricanes have won three straight, the last a 7-2 rout of Vancouver. The Capitals have won two in a row.
The Hurricanes pounce on loose pucks, and the Capitals cough them up. The Hurricanes and the Capitals sit at opposite ends for penalty kill.
